title: Cavity-control of Majorana bound states in superconductor-semiconductor heterostructures
authors: Francesco Buonemani, Massimo Balmelli, Olesia Dmytruk
abstract: We theoretically study a hybrid superconductor-semiconductor platform hosting Majorana bound states coupled to a single mode photonic cavity. Starting with a one-dimensional wire coupled to a bulk $s$-wave superconductor embedded in a photonic cavity, we derive an effective light-matter Hamiltonian for such a platform. Assuming that the photonic vector potential is aligned along the tunneling between a wire and a superconductor, we find that the cavity coupling enters only in the effective superconducting pairing term. By solving the coupled electron-photon Hamiltonian using different approaches, such as exact diagonalization in case of zero or large number of photons, high-frequency expansion, and mean-field decoupling, we find that the phase boundary between the topological trivial phases is shifted to smaller values of the Zeeman energy compared to the uncoupled case. Cavity embedding has the strongest effect on the phase diagram in the semiclassical regime, corresponding to a large number of photons. In all cases, we find that at large values of the light-matter coupling strength the effective superconducting pairing is suppressed, driving the system into the gapless phase. We demonstrate that even small light-matter coupling strength allows for entering the topological phase at values of the Zeeman energy compared to the uncoupled platform.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes Majorana bound states in a superconductor-semiconductor nanowire coupled to an optical cavity. By solving the coupled electron-photon Hamiltonian, the authors show that the cavity interaction modifies the topological phase diagram, enabling the topological state to be accessed at lower external magnetic fields than previously thought possible.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates how coupling Majorana bound states (MBSs) in a superconductor-semiconductor heterostructure to a single-mode photonic cavity modifies the system's topological phase diagram.
main_result: Cavity coupling shifts the phase boundary to smaller Zeeman energies, and even weak coupling allows entering the topological phase at lower critical Zeeman energies than the uncoupled case.
method: The authors derived an effective light-matter Hamiltonian and solved the coupled electron-photon system using exact diagonalization, high-frequency expansion, and mean-field decoupling.
model_or_system: The model is a hybrid platform: a 1D quantum wire tunnel-coupled to an s-wave superconductor, all embedded within a single-mode photonic cavity. The coupling enters the effective superconducting pairing term.
key_observables: Topological phase boundary, gap closing, effective superconducting pairing strength.
important_parameters: Light-matter coupling strength (g), Zeeman energy ($V_Z$), number of photons (n).
main_assumptions: The photonic vector potential is aligned along the tunneling direction, and the analysis uses approximations for the photon number (e.g., dark cavity limit or semiclassical limit).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the physical setup (wire-superconductor-cavity). Figure 2(a) shows the topological phase diagram dependence on $V_Z/\Delta_{eff}$ and $g$ for the dark cavity limit.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the coupled Hamiltonian, derives the effective wire-cavity Hamiltonian, and then applies various mathematical techniques (exact diagonalization, etc.) to calculate the phase diagram and analyze the impact of coupling strength.
why_interesting: This work directly combines concepts from cavity QED (light-matter coupling) with topological superconductivity, which is a major area of research in AMO physics and quantum optics.
